topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, introducing complement and framing the lecture's scope within immunology.

topics.label: Foundational concepts, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core principles, historical naming rules, and the central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the alternative, lectin, and classical recognition pathways operate and converge to reach the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary effector outcomes driven by complement activation to eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host tissues from accidental complement destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical manifestations and disease liabilities associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms pathogens deploy to circumvent complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, wrapping up the session and previewing the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
